vulnerability.title: Symfony HttpFoundation incorrectly parses PATH_INFO, returning URL paths without a leading slash and enabling limited authorization bypass

fixed_releases.verified_content: At v5.4.50 preparePathInfo prepends "/" whenever the substring after baseUrl does not start with it; fix 9962b91b is an ancestor of the tag and absent from v5.4.45
Same tree: tag v5.4.50 peels to 4b031a79 and contains the Request.php change from 9962b91b

fix_commits.message: [HttpFoundation] Fix parsing pathinfo with no leading slash

severity.numeric_level_rationale: CVSS 3.1 numeric 7.3 falls in High (7.0-8.9); the metric is supplied by the GitHub_M CNA and republished by NVD as its only, secondary metric, with low impact on all three properties
severity.source: GitHub advisory (GitHub_M CNA) CVSS 3.1 vector; NVD carries the same vector as a secondary metric only

vulnerability.category_l2: PATH_INFO computed after stripping the base URL is returned without a leading slash, so access-control rules that assume "/"-prefixed paths can be bypassed

critical_operation.description: preparePathInfo removes the computed base URL from the request URI and returns the remainder unchanged unless it is false or empty. Nothing forces the remainder to begin with "/", so a URI whose base URL ends mid-segment (for example "/api/index.phpfoo" with baseUrl "/api/index.php") yields pathInfo "foo". The 5.4.50 fix prefixes "/" whenever the remainder does not already start with it.

entry_point.description: getPathInfo(), reached from any HttpFoundation Request built from the PHP server variables, lazily calls preparePathInfo(); REQUEST_URI and SCRIPT_NAME are the request-controlled inputs used to compute requestUri and baseUrl.

trace.description: The Request is built from server variables and getRequestUri() returns REQUEST_URI with the query string still present
getPathInfo() lazily invokes preparePathInfo() to derive the path
preparePathInfo strips the base URL and returns a remainder that may not start with "/"

supports: preparePathInfo computes $pathInfo = substr($requestUri, strlen($baseUrl))
when the remainder is non-empty it is returned unchanged, with no check that it starts with "/"
for a request URI such as "/index.phpfoo" with baseUrl "/index.php" the method returns "foo" instead of "/foo"
at v5.4.50 preparePathInfo returns "/".$pathInfo whenever the remainder is false, empty or does not start with "/"
the returned path therefore always begins with "/" after the fix
the rest of preparePathInfo (query-string removal and baseUrl handling) is unchanged
the 5.4 patch replaces the two-branch empty check with "false === $pathInfo || '' === $pathInfo || '/' !== $pathInfo[0]" returning "/".$pathInfo
the patch adds a RequestTest case with request URI "/api/index.phpfoo" and baseUrl "/api/index.php" expecting pathInfo "/foo"
the patch touches only Request.php and RequestTest.php
the file opens with a PHP open tag and declares namespace Symfony\Component\HttpFoundation
the snapshot inventory records the HttpFoundation component as PHP

source_crosscheck.notes: All sources agree on affected <5.4.50 and on the missing leading-slash guarantee. NVD has no primary metric and republishes the CNA/GHSA 7.3 vector. The symfony.com and GHSA texts are identical. OSV ranges are the only machine-readable ranges and are consistent with the advisory pages.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read Request.php at v5.4.45 and confirm preparePathInfo returns a remainder without a leading slash.
An independent reviewer must confirm 9962b91b is absent from v5.4.45 and present in v5.4.50 with the leading-slash fix.
An independent reviewer must confirm the affected range includes 5.4.45 and the fixed release is 5.4.50.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.
No Symfony application, web server or PoC was executed; the finding is static.
The advisory describes the impact as bypassing "some" access-control rules that assume a leading slash; the exact set of affected access-control configurations was not enumerated.
Only the 5.4 branch was fetched and compared; the 6.4.29 and 7.3.7 fixes were not diffed.
NVD has no primary CVSS metric; the 7.3 vector is the GitHub advisory (GitHub_M CNA) metric, recorded as secondary by NVD.

The v5.4.45 blob differs from the fix patch pre-image because unrelated commits changed Request.php between v5.4.45 and the fix; equivalence was established on the preparePathInfo code block, not on blob identity.
open_questions: Which concrete Symfony security/access_control configurations (access_control path regexes, firewall request matchers) are bypassable with a slash-less path was not surveyed.
Whether front controllers or web servers normalize such URIs before PHP sees REQUEST_URI was not tested.
